events.event_hazard: Nuclear disaster (radiological contamination) triggered by the Great East Japan Earthquake and Tsunami
key_impacts: Large-scale nuclear disaster at TEPCO’s Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Plant, directly caused by the Great East Japan Earthquake and Tsunami of March 11, 2011.
Nuclear fuel melted inside reactors; the accident is not over and requires continuous cooling with circulating water.
Coolant water becomes extremely contaminated and leaks into the reactor building basements.
About 400 tons of groundwater flow into the site daily; the site is packed with 1,000‑ton capacity tanks storing contaminated water.
The ground beneath the tanks is not sturdy and tanks could topple; without continued cooling there is risk of further release of radioactive materials.
